newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian Hindu opposition emboldened by Rao's woes.
newsitem.headline: Indian Hindu opposition emboldened by Rao's woes.

text.p: India's Hindu nationalist opposition on Friday predicted former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao's legal troubles would create growing strains within the centre-left coalition government.

"Our confidence has gone up," L.K. Advani, president of the right-wing Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), said after Rao was charged in a forgery case and denied legal protection from arrest in a separate, criminal conspiracy case.
Rao's lawyer said on Thursday that he expected the former Congress party president to be arrested on Monday, when Rao has been ordered to appear in a Delhi court in the conspiracy case.
A court on Thursday rejected Rao's plea for anticipatory bail, which would have protected him against arrest. Legal experts said he could request ordinary bail if arrested on Monday.
The two others accused in the case of criminal conspiracy to cheat are currently under judicial custody in Tihar jail, Asia's biggest prison with some 10,000 inmates, awaiting trial.

Newspapers said authorities were preparing for the possibility the former prime minister might be arrested in the cheating case and put under police custody ahead of the trial. Rao has denied any involvement in the 13-year-old case.

The Asian Age daily said authorities were readying a bungalow in central Delhi as a "special prison" for Rao. One official said there was a possibility that Rao, if arrested, would be confined to his home.

Share prices on the Bombay Stock Exchange fell on the news that Rao had been charged in the forgery case and denied anticipatory bail. The exchange's benchmark index was down 41.95 points, or 1.27 percent, at 3,265.10 at 12:10 a.m. (0640 GMT).
Brokers said Rao's political worries and their potential effect on the coalition government had created uncertainty that undermined share prices.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's 13-party coalition lacks an outright majority in the 545-seat lower house of parliament and depends on the support of Congress's 140 deputies.
Congress finished second in general elections ended in May behind the BJP, which held power for 12 days before stepping down when it failed to muster enough support to win a confidence vote.
On Thursday Deve Gowda said he did not believe Rao's resignation last Saturday as Congress president would upset his United Front coalition government.

"Why do you worry?" Deve Gowda asked reporters after taking oath as a member of the upper house. "They (Congress) have not created any problems for our government so far and we are hopeful the same policy will continue."

But senior BJP leader Jaswant Singh, who served as finance minister in the short-lived BJP government, said the charges against Rao spelled trouble for the United Front, especially in local polls in populous Uttar Pradesh starting next week.

"An event of this kind, following the other difficulties the Congress party is facing, must surely tell and the only manner in which it can tell is in the inter-relationship between Congress and the United Front," Singh told Reuters.
"This is a very unreal and unequal relationship. When both parties come under strain, there will be either further weakness or they come apart. There is no third option," he said.
The new Congress chief, Sitaram Kesri, asked if Rao's woes had affected is party, said: "I can't deny (it)."
